Content: 🇬🇧 The UK isn’t hiring fewer Data Engineers. It’s hiring differently. Over the past few months, one trend has become difficult to ignore. Many UK employers are no longer looking for specialists in a single tool. They’re looking for professionals who can work across the modern Microsoft data stack. A typical Data Engineer vacancy today is more likely to ask for a combination of: • SQL • Azure Data Factory / Azure Data Services • Microsoft Fabric • Databricks • Power BI • Python This reflects how organisations are modernising their data platforms and combining analytics, engineering, and cloud capabilities into unified teams. OLAP is the giant history book used for deep, analytical research later. 🔹 Star vs. Snowflake Schema: How we organize data tables. Star is simple and direct; Snowflake is highly organized but more complex. ​Every master was once a beginner. Hôm nay đến ngày 3: Chuẩn OECD nói gì? Thật ra không khó như anh chị nghĩ Mỗi lần nghe đến cụm từ "chuẩn quản trị quốc tế" hay "OECD", nhiều chủ doanh nghiệp thường có chung một phản ứng: "Chắc cái này dành cho tập đoàn lớn." Nếu bỏ hết những từ ngữ học thuật đi, chuẩn OECD chỉ đang trả lời một câu hỏi rất đơn giản: Doanh nghiệp của mình có đang được vận hành một cách công bằng và minh bạch hay chưa? Nếu công ty có nhiều cổ đông, những người góp vốn nhỏ có được cập nhật tình hình kinh doanh đầy đủ không, hay chỉ người thân của chủ doanh nghiệp mới biết mọi chuyện? Báo cáo tài chính có phản ánh đúng thực tế để mọi người cùng nhìn vào và ra quyết định, hay chỉ làm cho đủ hồ sơ? Khi giám đốc đưa ra một quyết định lớn, có ai đủ vai trò để phản biện, góp ý hay giám sát không? Hay cuối cùng vẫn là "sếp quyết sao thì vậy"? Đó đều là những điều OECD nhắc đến. Nghe có vẻ lớn lao, nhưng thực chất chỉ xoay quanh vài nguyên tắc rất đời thường: - Đối xử công bằng với các cổ đông. - Công khai thông tin đầy đủ và đúng thời điểm. - Hội đồng quản trị hoặc người có trách nhiệm phải thực hiện đúng vai trò giám sát. - Tôn trọng quyền lợi của nhân viên, khách hàng, đối tác và các bên liên quan. - Xây dựng một hệ thống quản trị minh bạch để doanh nghiệp không phụ thuộc vào một cá nhân. Trung thấy đây là điểm sáng Trung thấy hay "nhì" trong các chuẩn quốc tế, để DN có thêm một "tấm gương" để soi lại doanh nghiệp của mình. Đọc xong là sure biết DN mạnh yếu chỗ nào và nên cải thiện điều gì trước. Rất nhiều doanh nghiệp không gặp vấn đề vì thiếu doanh thu. Họ gặp vấn đề vì mọi thứ đang vận hành bằng niềm tin, bằng kinh nghiệm của một người, chứ chưa có quy trình rõ ràng. Đến khi doanh nghiệp lớn hơn hoặc muốn gọi vốn, những điểm yếu đó mới bắt đầu lộ ra. Nếu có AI hỗ trợ, bạn cũng không cần đọc hàng trăm trang tài liệu để hiểu các nguyên tắc này. Content: Le informazioni sono ovunque: il problema è trovarle 🚀 Parliamo spesso di investimenti, budget e strategie, ma raramente del costo più silenzioso e logorante: il tempo sprecato a cercare risposte. Ogni giorno le aziende generano un enorme bagaglio di conoscenze: documenti, email, report, procedure e quando tutto questo è sparso su mille piattaforme finisce per restare nascosto. E così invece di lavorare, si cerca. Si aprono decine di cartelle, si sfogliano vecchie conversazioni, si chiede ai colleghi se ricordano dove sia un file o chi abbia l'ultima versione di un documento. Minuti che sembrano irrilevanti ma che sommati diventano ore perse ogni settimana. Il punto è che non basta avere tante informazioni, serve poterle trovare nel momento in cui servono, senza dover interrompere il flusso di lavoro e senza dipendere sempre da qualcuno che "sa dove guardare". Quando la conoscenza interna è organizzata e accessibile, cambia il modo di lavorare: le risposte arrivano più velocemente, le attività si sbloccano prima e le decisioni vengono prese con maggiore consapevolezza. E soprattutto succede una cosa semplice ma spesso sottovalutata: si smette di perdere tempo ed energie in ciò che non dovrebbe richiederne. Il lavoro torna ad essere lavoro e non una continua caccia alle informazioni. Il tempo delle persone ha un valore e sprecarlo a cercare ciò che dovrebbe essere già a portata di mano è un costo che nessuna azienda dovrebbe considerare normale. Ogni minuto risparmiato nella ricerca di un'informazione è un minuto restituito alle persone. Perché il valore del lavoro non si misura dal tempo impiegato a cercare una risposta ma da quello che si riesce a costruire una volta trovata. While it works well for general context, the lossy compression can cause errors with exact values like IDs, hashes, or secrets, making it best suited for non-critical information. Content: Imagine a phone with no apps. No home screen grid, no app drawer, no navigation menus. Just a single text field. That's AppLess, an experimental mobile app from Thesys. You type what you want — "find me a flight to Chicago" — and the interface streams into existence as native components. Departure times, airline logos, a booking button. All generated on the fly by an LLM. The catch? Nothing actually works. Every action is simulated. The flight was never booked. The confirmation is fiction. But here's what makes this interesting: the rendering pipeline is real and surprisingly efficient. The team built a thin native runtime using a compact DSL called openui-lang that uses roughly half the tokens of comparable JSON formats. Screens render as Cupertino widgets on iOS and Material 3 on Android from the same model output. The architecture is remarkably thin. A single component contract file defines every UI element the model is allowed to use. No hallucinated buttons, no imaginary sliders. Just a direct pipeline from natural language to native UI, running entirely on-device with no backend. The project is MIT-licensed with five concrete fork ideas. Thesys built the shell. They're daring developers to wire it to real data. The gap between plausible fiction and functional interface might be narrower than it looks. Content: Spent an hour last week trying to get a 14B local model to do something a five-line script could've done in ten seconds. That's the trap. Once a multi-agent pipeline is running, everything starts looking like an agent problem. The actual skill isn't building bigger pipelines. It's knowing when a tool needs real care, adversarial review, confidence checks, a human on the diff, and when simple deterministic code is not just enough but better, because it never hallucinates. Every task handed to a model instead of a script is attention not spent on the decisions that need a human. Which model to trust unsupervised. When a suspiciously clean confidence result should worry you instead of relieve you. Good judgement isn't using AI everywhere. It's knowing exactly where not to. Content: Most AI can read financial documents today. That hasn’t been the hard part for a while. The real challenge is what comes after: turning a document into data a finance team can actually trust — traceable, validated, and ready to fit into a workflow without someone re-checking every field. “The model was pretty sure” doesn’t survive an audit. It was encouraging to see this direction reflected in Microsoft’s latest Build 2026 write-up on Azure Content Understanding, combining document AI with LLM reasoning to produce structured, grounded outputs, not just raw text. FinHero gets a mention there for exactly this shift, moving from traditional extraction to reliable, workflow-ready understanding. That’s the whole reason FinXtract MCP exists. Not “can the model read it,” but “can a finance team act on it without second-guessing.” The next phase of document intelligence won’t be won by the most capable model. It will be won by whoever makes the output structured, traceable, and reliable enough that finance teams stop thinking about the AI at all. Content: 🚀 Understanding Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD) in Data Engineering Have you ever wondered how companies track customer information when it changes over time without losing the previous data? That's where Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD) come in. 📖 SCD Types Explained 🟢 Type 0 – Fixed ✔ Data never changes. ✔ Best for static reference data. 🟣 Type 1 – Overwrite ✔ Updates the existing record. ❌ No history is maintained. 🔵 Type 2 – Add New Row ⭐ (Most Used) ✔ Creates a new record for every change. ✔ Preserves complete historical data. ✔ Ideal for analytics, reporting, and auditing. 🟠 Type 3 – Add New Column ✔ Stores only the previous value. ✔ Maintains limited history. 💡 Why Every Data Engineer Should Know SCD ✅ Historical Data Tracking ✅ Accurate Business Reports ✅ Regulatory Compliance ✅ Better Customer Insights ✅ Trend Analysis ✅ Data Lineage & Governance ✅ Smarter Business Decisions 🎯 Interview Tip Which SCD type is most commonly used? 👉 SCD Type 2 Because businesses need complete historical records for analytics, auditing, and compliance. 💬 Which SCD Type have you implemented in your project? Content: Power BI on top of Snowflake is either the best decision you'll make this year or a very expensive way to hide a data model problem. Here's the tell. If your report is slow and the fix everyone proposes is a bigger warehouse, stop. Compute is rarely the issue. I've watched a team double their Snowflake spend to speed up a dashboard that was slow because it joined six tables at render time to rebuild a number that should have been modeled once, upstream. Power BI is very good at making a bad model feel survivable. That's the trap. It papers over the problem just well enough that nobody fixes it, and the bill grows quietly until someone in finance asks a question nobody can answer. The honest test: can you explain your top metric's lineage in one sentence? If not, the problem isn't the BI tool. Model first. Visualize second. Every time we've done it in that order at SourceMash, the warehouse bill went down, not up. Content: 🚀 SQL Bootcamp 30 | Day 12 🎓 Learn SQL with 🔹 SELF JOIN A SELF JOIN joins a table with itself using table aliases. Common Uses: Employee–Manager relationships Organizational hierarchy Finding duplicate records Comparing rows within the same table 🔹 CROSS JOIN A CROSS JOIN returns the Cartesian product of two tables. Every row from the first table is combined with every row from the second table. Common Uses: Product combinations Test data generation Scheduling Matrix reports ✍️ Key Differences ✔ SELF JOIN uses the same table twice. ✔ CROSS JOIN combines every row from both tables. ✔ SELF JOIN requires aliases to distinguish the tables. ✔ CROSS JOIN does not require a join condition. ✔ Both are frequently asked in SQL interviews. 💻 See It in Action -- SELF JOIN SELECT e1.Name AS Employee, e2.Name AS Manager FROM Employees e1 JOIN Employees e2 ON e1.ManagerID = e2.EmployeeID; -- CROSS JOIN SELECT p.ProductName, c.Color FROM Products p CROSS JOIN Colors c; 🌍 Where Are They Used? 👨‍💼 Employee–Manager hierarchy 🛍️ Product & Variant combinations 📊 Reporting & Analytics 🧪 Test Data Generation 🏭 Manufacturing (Bill of Materials) ☁️ Data Engineering & ETL ⭐ Why Should You Learn Them? ✔ Compare records within the same table ✔ Generate all possible combinations ✔ Solve real-world hierarchy problems ✔ Improve SQL problem-solving skills ✔ Commonly asked in SQL interviews 🚫 Common Mistakes ❌ Forgetting to use aliases in SELF JOIN ❌ Using CROSS JOIN on large tables without understanding the result size ❌ Confusing SELF JOIN with INNER JOIN ❌ Forgetting that CROSS JOIN can return a massive number of rows 💎 Pro SQL Tip SELF JOIN is an interviewer favorite for Employee–Manager and hierarchy-based questions. Content: Kafka Performance Tuning: Optimizing Throughput, Latency, and Scalability Running Kafka in production isn't just about deployment, it's about continuous performance optimization to handle millions of events reliably. Here are some proven tuning strategies: Optimize Producers: Increase batch size, enable compression, configure acknowledgments (acks) wisely, and tune linger.ms. Tune Brokers: Balance replication factor, optimize log segments, use SSD storage, and configure network threads efficiently. Improve Consumers: Increase fetch size, manage offsets effectively, and tune session timeouts for faster recovery. Scale with Partitions: Add partitions strategically to improve parallelism while ensuring balanced key distribution. Monitor Everything: Track throughput, latency, consumer lag, CPU, memory, disk I/O, and network utilization using monitoring dashboards. Production Best Practices: Perform load testing, automate scaling, secure clusters, and schedule regular maintenance to maintain peak performance. A well-tuned Kafka cluster delivers higher throughput, lower latency, improved fault tolerance, and effortless scalability, making it the backbone of modern event-driven architectures. Content: 📢 Google將NotebookLM改名為Gemini Notebook Google於美國時間7月16日正式宣布，將旗下人工智能研究工具NotebookLM改名為Gemini Notebook，此舉屬品牌整合，並非推出全新產品，用戶原有筆記、資料及功能將完整保留。Google在官方部落格表示，Gemini Notebook仍將維持獨立產品定位，繼續作為用戶研究的首選工具，但未來會在Google整體生態系統中扮演更重要角色，包括與Gemini應用程式及Google搜尋作更深度整合。 🕰️ 品牌統一背後的發展歷程 Gemini Notebook前身NotebookLM於2023年以「Project Tailwind」為代號啟動，並在當年Google I/O大會首度亮相，定位為協助整理及理解資料的研究助手。同年7月起開放候補名單申請，隨後率先於美國推出，並逐步擴展至全球市場，功能亦不斷擴充。此次改名後，介面標誌亦換上與Gemini系列一致的藍紫漸層設計，以配合Google整體人工智能品牌形象。 🔗 維持獨立產品定位 儘管更名，Gemini Notebook並不會被併入Gemini聊天機械人主體，而是繼續以獨立研究工具形式運作，惟兩者之間的內容將可同步使用。有外媒指出，由於Gemini應用程式本身亦已具備筆記本功能，故此次整合或會令部分用戶對兩者關係感到混淆，但Google強調兩個版本的筆記本是互相連結及同步的。Google方面預告，未來Gemini Notebook的內容將逐步整合至Google搜尋的AI模式（AI Mode），惟暫未公布具體時間表。 💻 新增雲端運算及分析功能 除品牌更名外，Google亦為Gemini Notebook引入代號為「安全雲端電腦」的新功能，讓用戶可直接在筆記本內編寫及執行程式碼，進行更深入的資料分析工作，例如根據上傳文件生成統計摘要。此項功能率先向Google AI Ultra及Workspace商業版用戶開放，Google表示將於未來數周內逐步擴展至網頁版AI Pro用戶，並支援更多輸出格式。 📈 使用規模龐大 涵蓋教育及企業界 根據Google公布數字，Gemini Notebook（前稱NotebookLM）目前已錄得超過3,000萬名使用者，以及逾60萬個機構或組織使用，應用範圍涵蓋學生課堂筆記整理，以至企業新員工入職培訓資料製作。工具核心功能包括自動生成資料摘要，以及根據使用者提供的內容製作音訊與視訊概述，協助用戶更有效率地消化及傳遞知識。 ✅ 對現有用戶影響輕微 多家科技媒體分析指出，此次更動對一般用戶而言學習成本極低，因原有筆記本內容、功能及操作方式基本維持不變，系統將自動重新導向，確保現有共用連結及筆記本正常運作。Google Workspace更新頁面亦指出，管理員無需採取任何行動，新名稱及標誌將於未來數星期內，透過網頁及流動應用程式版本逐步向全球用戶推出。 內容由 AI Marketer HK 製作 ———— 👇 相信「AI × 數碼營銷」是未來的你， 歡迎 Tag 一位同行好友，一起成長！ AIMarketerHK DigitalMarketing Gemini GeminiNotebook NotebookLM

Content: Tens of thousands of AI prompts. Now running on Microsoft's own model. Microsoft just quietly redirected a massive chunk of its AI workload in Excel and Outlook away from OpenAI and Anthropic, routing it through its own in-house MAI models instead. The reason? Microsoft's AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman put it plainly: the goal is to "reduce and ultimately eliminate" the cost of paying third-party AI providers. This is the build-vs-buy question playing out in real time, at the largest scale possible. Every enterprise that has woven third-party AI APIs into its workflows is carrying a version of this risk: dependency on vendors whose pricing, availability, and priorities are outside your control. Microsoft had the runway to build its way out. Most organisations don't. But the question it raises is worth putting on the table: how embedded are you in any single AI vendor's ecosystem, and what does your contingency look like if that changes? Content: I used to ship 2-3 features a week. Now it is 2-3 a day. Same models. Same codebase. Same developer. Here is what changed. Every session with an AI agent started from zero. It did not know my architecture, my design system, or my rules. So it built things that looked right and were wrong. Wrong folder, wrong pattern, hardcoded strings that should have been translation keys, no tests. I spent more time correcting it than the work would have taken me. The model was never the problem. I was asking a capable engineer to work on a large codebase with no onboarding, and doing it again every morning. So I stopped, and I built the onboarding. Docs written for agents instead of humans. A memory directory the agent writes to itself, so what it learns survives the session. Then seven custom Claude Code skills, one per workflow. Entry point, new features, testing, localization, git commits, hydration, docs and memory sync. The entry point is the one that changed everything. Every task starts there. It reads the rules, opens the memory index, loads only the docs that task needs, then routes to the rest. But my favorite part is not a skill. It is a hook. A Stop hook checks whether code changed without docs or memory changing with it. If it did, it blocks the agent from ending the turn. The agent is not allowed to say done. That is not a line in a README nobody reads. It is a shell script. The workflow now: Opus 4.8 plans it, Sonnet 5 subagents build it, Opus reviews them, a code-reviewer skill checks for bugs and security, then I read every line. Opus is expensive. Sonnet is not. Planning is where the expensive model earns its money. Typing is not. Everyone has the same models. Content: SaaS metrics are dead. OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar just published a new framework for measuring AI ROI, and it challenges the foundational metric of the last 20 years: user seat licenses. Since AI performs the actual work—rather than just assisting humans—measuring user adoption is the wrong target. Instead, Friar proposes a new North Star: "Useful Intelligence per Dollar." Here is the 4-pillar scorecard OpenAI uses to track AI value: 1. Task completion effectiveness: Does the AI actually finish the job? (e.g., customer tickets resolved, code changes shipped). 2. Cost per successful task: The total economic efficiency of achieving a successful outcome—not just the raw cost per token. 3. Dependability: Can users rely on the results? (This accounts for retries, error recovery, and human oversight). 4. Value scalability: Does the investment produce more value as usage grows, without costs spiraling out of control? The true price of AI includes the cost of failures. A cheaper, less dependable model that requires human intervention or five retries is actually more expensive than a premium frontier model that succeeds on the first try. Stop counting tokens. Start measuring outcomes. Read the full framework: openai.com/index/a-scorecard-for-the-ai-age — If you're here for signal—not hype—you're in the right place. Content: 🔥 Mozilla's first State of Open Source AI report just dropped and the numbers hit hard. Open models trail closed ones by 3.3 percentage points on benchmarks but handle 33% of production tokens while capturing only 4% of revenue. Think about that gap. You're running inference, paying compute costs, shipping real traffic on open weights. And the money still flows to closed labs charging roughly 6x more per call for comparable quality. Operational costs for open models fell 50x in three years, yet only 51% of teams using open weights actually reach production compared to 63% on closed models. The performance gap isn't what's blocking you. It's deployment tooling. Mistral hit $400M ARR growing twentyfold in 12 months. Databricks is at $5.4B. The commercial layer is real. My agency routes high-volume workloads to open models whenever the task doesn't need advanced reasoning. And the savings are immediate. Audit where your tokens actually go this week. You're probably paying closed prices for work an open model already handles. Content: Connecting enterprise systems doesn't have to mean writing thousands of lines of integration code. That's where Apache Kafka Connect transforms modern data engineering. Instead of building and maintaining custom pipelines, Kafka Connect offers ready-to-use source and sink connectors for databases, REST APIs, cloud storage, search engines, and enterprise applications. Key benefits: Integrate databases like MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Oracle Connect cloud platforms such as AWS S3 and Azure services Stream data from REST APIs and third-party applications Enable scalable, fault-tolerant data pipelines Configure integrations with simple JSON instead of custom code Support both real-time streaming and batch workloads Maintain schema consistency using Schema Registry Whether you're building ETL pipelines, event-driven microservices, IoT platforms, analytics systems, or data lakes, Kafka Connect dramatically reduces development effort while improving reliability and scalability. Understanding Kafka Connect is an essential skill for every modern Data Engineer, Backend Developer, and Cloud Architect working with real-time data ecosystems. Content: Most people think great content is all about using the right keywords. It isn't. The best-performing content is written for people first and optimized for search engines second. Over the years, I've learned that small improvements in your writing style can make a huge difference in rankings, engagement, and conversions. Here's what actually works: 1- Hook people in the first 2 lines. If you don't, they scroll. Simple as that. 2- Answer the main question immediately. Don't make people wait for the "good part." 3- Keep your paragraphs short. One idea per line. Nobody's reading a wall of text on their phone. 4- Use bullet points. They're scannable. They save time. People love that. 5- Break the pattern sometimes. Say something unexpected. Surprise your reader mid-post. 6- Write like you're talking to ONE person. Not a crowd. Not an audience. One human being. 7- Cut the fluff. If a sentence doesn't add value, delete it. No mercy. 8- Make your FAQs actually useful. Not the generic ones everyone copies. 9- Add a quick summary box. Some people just want the TL;DR. Give it to them. 10- And always, always end with something actionable. Give people a next step. Great content doesn't just rank—it builds trust, solves problems, and converts readers into customers. Content: Retro yang gak pernah bikin tim berubah itu masalah klasik project AI. Kalau temen-temen manage tim AI dan menemukan action item dari retrospective itu-itu aja yang balik lagi tiap sprint tanpa pernah beres, masalahnya bukan di format retronya. Masalahnya, action item retro diperlakukan sebagai catatan, bukan kerjaan beneran. Task fitur punya owner, estimasi, dan masuk sprint backlog. Action item retro nggak punya siapa-siapa, nggak punya deadline, dan nggak pernah masuk ke tempat tim kerja sehari-hari. Wajar kalau improvement internal terus kalah sama kerjaan yang keliatan. Perbaikannya: kasih tiap action item satu owner yang jelas, masukin ke sprint backlog yang sama dengan task fitur, batasi jumlahnya, dan mulai tiap retro dengan review action item sebelumnya. Ukuran sukses retro bukan berapa insight yang muncul, tapi berapa perubahan yang beneran kejadian.
